S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: Two years ago, Titus Griffin was made acting shift lead at the retail store, a step toward management that required him to handle after-hours inventory counts in the stockroom and inspect the narrow service stairwell and loading area before closing. After an early night when a bat got into the back corridor during a receiving shift, he began developing a marked fear of bats and similar sudden fluttering movement, far beyond the actual likelihood of danger in the store. Over the full 2 years and 0 months, the fear became clinically significant because he increasingly traded closing duties, avoided parts of the stockroom during evening shifts, and endured required checks with intense fear, putting his promotion plans and reliability at work at risk. He eventually sought psychiatric care through his employer’s assistance program after his store manager documented that the avoidance was interfering with his readiness for a permanent management role.

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: I know a bat in the store probably isn't going to hurt me, but if I see anything that looks like one or even a quick flutter in the back hallway, my mind treats it like I'm in real danger.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: What brings me in is that the second I think there might be a bat or something flapping around the stockroom, my heart jumps, I start sweating, and I feel like I need to get out right then.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I've been swapping out closing shifts, taking the long way around the loading area, and when I have to check the stairwell I make myself do it fast while holding my phone and feeling scared the whole time.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My manager has started questioning whether I can handle the shift lead role because I keep trading closing duties and I'm not as dependable for the after-hours checks. It feels like this could cost me the permanent management position I was working toward.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about two years, since that night a bat got into the back corridor during a receiving shift.
